knowledge_misuse: Utilisation ratios 0.67/0.56 are attributed to 'REF-TI-TIDA-010054 decision 1'; Decision 1 in the analysis is the DAB topology and the file names neither the devices nor the ratios. They are AIPE-derived from the device choices recorded in SKILL-006 principle 1 (EC-019/EC-020); TI states no derating rule, so they are weak evidence for the 80/90/70 % limits (which the agent correctly labels as judgement for human review).

KR-GD-003: the parasitic-turn-on immunity figure (1.3 V) is computed with the small-signal C_rss at 1000 V, which understates the Miller charge by roughly a factor of four; the clamp is presented as 'recommended' with a 'large margin' although a charge-based estimate leaves about 1 V or less. The rule's exclusion (clamp not strictly needed with low R_G and low-inductance routing) is not shown to apply.
KR-PCB-004 is a layout optimisation objective and carries no inductance value; the 25/35 nH figures are the agent's own assumption (correctly labelled) and must not be read as knowledge-derived.

KR-GD-006 is applied across generations of a single supplier whereas its condition names multi-sourced suppliers; the rationale covers generations, so this is an acceptable low-priority extension, noted only.

No reference instance values were copied (6.4 V / 1 us DESAT, 2 ohm R_G, 0.1 K/W pad, 40 degC ambient, 50/69 W limits were all replaced by design-specific values); human-review rules KR-TH-002, KR-PR-001, KR-GD-004 were surfaced, not decided.
required_changes: Replace the k_RG = 1.3 switching-energy factor with values read from the C4MS025120K E_on/E_off versus R_G figures (Fig. 29/31) at the chosen R_G,on/off, or present the high-side switching loss as a 9.8-15 W range (k 1.3-2.0) and the MOSFET total as 46.7-52 W (0.93-1.04 %) until the double-pulse test; propagate the range to the efficiency budget.
Add the high-side device's own output-capacitance loss E_oss(400 V) x fs (about 1 W) and correct the statement that the measured E_on contains the C_oss energy of both devices.

Redo the parasitic turn-on check with a charge-based method (Q_gd(0-400 V) about 20-27 nC, C_gs about 3.08 nF, 5.6 ohm off path, 8-13 ns transition -> 4.5-5.2 V excursion, V_GS about +0.5 to +1.2 V) using the hot V_GS(th) minimum; state the Miller clamp as a requirement pending the PRD-09301 section 6.1 measurement and repeat for the C3M0021120K fallback (Q_gd 50 nC, C_rss 12 pF).

Update the thermal check with the thermal agent's selected hardware (R_th,HS 0.68 K/W forced, pad 0.63-0.82 K/W): T_J,HS about 124 degC and P_max 38.9 W at 440 V/27.5 A; state that the stacked worst case (max R_DS(on), k_RG 2.0) reaches about 150 degC in steady state and is mitigated only by the 10 s overload duration; drop or relabel the 52.4 W figure.
Reconcile the dead time with the assumptions agent (A-17: 200 ns initial): restate P_dt as 2.3 W (25 A) / 2.5 W (27.5 A) or document why the 250 ns envelope is kept.
Label the 37.0 mohm 'maximum at 15 V' as derived (28 x 33/25); correct the max-R text factor from 1.21 to 1.32.

State in the method that Q_rr of the C3M candidates was scaled by I_on/I_test, and note that SiC body-diode Q_rr is mostly capacitive so those LS recovery figures (and the C4MS E_rr scaled from a 15.8 A/ns test) are lower bounds with about a factor-two uncertainty.

Correct the citation of the utilisation ratios (derived from the TIDA device choices via SKILL-006 principle 1 / EC-019-020, not a TI 'decision 1' statement) and keep the 80/90/70 % limits explicitly as human-review judgement.
Use V_SD at 29-32 A (datasheet Fig. 8-10) rather than the 19.6 A point for the dead-time loss, and the 175 degC V_GS(th) for the Miller margin.
Verify whether Wolfspeed offers a Gen-4 750 V TO-247-4 family; if so, evaluate it as the natural class for the 440-480 V corners before finalising the 1200 V selection.
In the paralleling comparison, note that E_on and E_rr rise with doubled C_oss/Q_rr (31.4 W is a lower bound); the single-device conclusion stands.
summary: The selection of the Wolfspeed C4MS025120K (1200 V Gen-4, TO-247-4, one per position) is defensible and every stated calculation reproduces from the stated inputs: operating points, RMS and switching currents, R_DS(on)(150 degC) 48.5 mohm, conduction 15.3 W, HS switching 9.8 W, LS recovery 3.5 W, dead-time 2.9 W, totals 45.5-56.2 W over the six corners, 46.7 W = 0.93 % at 400 V/25 A, utilisation 42/44 % (650 V class 77-84 %), and the thermal arithmetic (104 degC, 52.4 W). The selected device's and the C3M0021120K fallback's datasheet values were verified from the fetched PDFs and the C3M0030090K obsolescence from the product page; the other 13 candidates and all stock/price data remain unverified. Corrections are needed in method and cross-area consistency rather than in the decision: the k_RG = 1.3 factor is optimistic (datasheet E-vs-R_G curves exist; k = 2.0 gives 52 W / 1.04 %), the DUT E_oss term (about 1 W) is wrongly argued away, the parasitic turn-on margin is overstated by using the 1000 V C_rss (a Q_gd-based estimate leaves about 1 V, so the Miller clamp should be mandatory pending measurement), the thermal inputs (0.5/0.5 K/W) are more optimistic than the thermal agent's selected sink and pad (0.68 / 0.63-0.82 K/W -> T_J about 124 degC, P_max 38.9 W; stacked worst case about 150 degC), the dead time (250 ns) conflicts with the assumptions agent's 200 ns, the 37.0 mohm 15 V maximum is derived not printed, the text factor 1.21 should read 1.32, and the utilisation-ratio citation to TIDA 'decision 1' is inaccurate. Human-review items (utilisation limits, KR-PR-001 timing, KR-GD-004 DESAT, KR-TH-002 pad rating, efficiency allocation, procurement) were correctly surfaced and no reference instance values were copied.
